issues_detected.description: The custom license and agreement are named, but the record explains eligibility for access without stating substantive reuse permissions.

issues_detected.recommendation: Analyze downstream benefits and harms of pediatric screening and other intended AI uses, including affected groups and practical mitigations.

semantic_insights: All evidence was assessed within the complete root datasheet. File collections contribute evidence to that root and were not scored as separate datasets.

Substantive root-level descriptions were credited where they directly satisfied an item's intent, including platform access, hosting, release changes, acquisition instruments, research objectives, and feature-quality issues.
The record consistently separates the registered-access feature release from the controlled raw-audio source and does not imply that raw recordings are included in the PhysioNet files.

Source caveats distinguish pediatric release facts from adult documentation and umbrella-protocol provisions. Protocol statements were not treated as independent proof that planned procedures were completed.

Eight internal consistency checks passed: identifier agreement; version agreement across fields; release-date ordering and issued-date agreement; stable participant coverage across the minor update; compatibility of differing feature counts with documented generation failures; human-subjects oversight and consent; funding-purpose alignment; and separation of feature and raw-audio access routes.
The grant caveat distinguishes separate NIH supplements rather than assigning all project-level funding references to this release.
The absence of applicability declarations was not filled from record content. Every conditional item remained unknown and scored.
Format checks were limited to the supplied text. DOI resolution, award existence, URL reachability, and the alternate latest-version DOI target were not externally verified.
